1.question: How many days of annual leave do I get after my probation ends?
1.answer: After completing probation, full-time employees receive 20 working days of paid annual leave per calendar year. This rises to 25 working days once you have more than 5 years of continuous service, and part-time employees receive leave in proportion to their contracted hours. Public holidays are in addition to this leave.

citations.quote: Full-time employees receive **20 working days** of paid annual leave per calendar year after completing probation.
Employees with more than 5 years of continuous service receive **25 working days**.
Part-time employees receive leave in proportion to their contracted hours.
Public holidays are in addition to annual leave.

2.question: How many unused leave days can I carry over into next year, and when do I have to use them?
2.answer: You can carry over up to 5 unused annual leave days into the next calendar year. Those carried-over days must be used by 31 March, or they are lost. Any days above the 5-day limit are lost at the end of the year unless the Head of People approves an exception in writing.

citations.quote: Up to **5 unused days** may be carried over into the next calendar year.
Carried-over days must be used by **31 March**; any carried-over days not used by then are lost.
Days above the 5-day limit are lost at the end of the year unless the Head of People approves an exception in writing.

3.question: When do I need a medical certificate for sick leave?
3.answer: You need a medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner if you are absent for more than 2 consecutive working days. In other words, an absence of 3 or more consecutive working days requires one.

citations.quote: A medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner is required for any absence of **more than 2 consecutive working days**.

4.question: Which days am I expected to be in the office?
4.answer: If you are in a hybrid role, you must work from the Lagos office at least 2 days per week, and Tuesday and Thursday are anchor days when all hybrid staff are expected in the office. You may work other days from home if your line manager agrees.

citations.quote: Employees in hybrid roles work from the Lagos office at least **2 days per week**.
**Tuesday and Thursday** are anchor days: all hybrid staff are expected in the office on these days.
Other days may be worked from home with the line manager's agreement.

5.question: How far in advance do I need to request an international trip?
5.answer: International travel must be requested at least 21 days before departure, and bookings go through the Travel Desk. If you request later than that, the request may be refused or may need Director approval.

citations.quote: International travel must be requested at least **21 days** before departure.
All flights and hotels are booked through the Travel Desk (travel@kestrelnova.example).
Late requests may be refused or may need Director approval.

6.question: What is the deadline for submitting an expense claim?
6.answer: You must submit expense claims in the Spendly expense tool within 30 days of the expense. Also note the payment timing: approved claims submitted before the 20th of the month are paid with that month's payroll, while those submitted on or after the 20th are paid in the following month's payroll.

citations.quote: Submit claims in the Spendly expense tool within **30 days** of the expense.
Approved claims submitted **before the 20th** of the month are paid with that month's payroll.
Claims submitted on or after the 20th are paid in the following month's payroll.

7.question: I lost my work laptop. What should I do?
7.answer: Report the lost laptop to IT Support at it-support@kestrelnova.example within 24 hours. IT will then remotely lock and wipe the device. If the laptop was stolen rather than lost, you must also report it to the police and share the report reference with IT.

citations.quote: Report a lost or stolen device to IT Support (it-support@kestrelnova.example) **within 24 hours**.
IT will remotely lock and wipe the device.
Theft must also be reported to the police, and the report reference shared with IT.

8.question: What is my yearly budget for training and courses?
8.answer: As a permanent employee, you have a learning budget of NGN 400,000 per calendar year for courses, certifications, conferences and books. Any unused budget does not carry over to the next year.

citations.quote: Each permanent employee has a learning budget of **NGN 400,000 per calendar year** for courses, certifications, conferences and books.
Unused budget does not carry over.

9.question: How much paternity leave do I get?
9.answer: You get 10 working days of paternity leave at full pay. You must take it within 3 months of your child's birth or adoption, and you can split it into up to two blocks.

citations.quote: Fathers and partners receive **10 working days** of paternity leave at full pay.
It must be taken within **3 months** of the child's birth or adoption and may be taken in up to two blocks.

10.question: A supplier sent me a gift worth NGN 25,000. Can I keep it?
10.answer: Not automatically. Your gift is worth NGN 25,000, which is above the NGN 15,000 limit for accepting gifts without declaration. You must declare it to Compliance (compliance@kestrelnova.example) within 5 working days, and Compliance will decide whether you may keep it, return it or donate it. If the gift is cash, a voucher or a gift card, it must never be accepted, whatever its value.

citations.quote: Gifts with a value of up to **NGN 15,000** may be accepted without declaration.
Gifts above NGN 15,000 must be **declared to Compliance within 5 working days** (compliance@kestrelnova.example). Compliance decides whether the gift may be kept, returned or donated.
Cash, vouchers and gift cards must never be accepted, whatever the value.

11.question: I stayed in a hotel costing NGN 70,000 per night on a domestic work trip. Is that within the limit, and who needs to approve my claim?
11.answer: Yes. NGN 70,000 per night is within the domestic hotel limit of NGN 80,000 per night. Because the amount is above NGN 50,000, your claim needs approval from both your line manager and Finance.

citations.quote: - Domestic hotels: maximum **NGN 80,000 per night**.
- Items **above NGN 50,000**: line manager **and** Finance approval.

12.question: The company paid NGN 300,000 for my certification. If I resign 8 months after finishing it, what do I owe, and what happens to my unused annual leave?
12.answer: Your certification cost NGN 300,000, which is more than the NGN 200,000 threshold. Eight months is within the 12-month window, so you would have to repay 50% of the cost, which is NGN 150,000. Where possible, this amount is deducted from your final salary. Any accrued but unused annual leave for the current year is paid out at your basic daily rate in your final salary.

citations.quote: If the company pays for a single course or certification costing **more than NGN 200,000**, and the employee resigns within **12 months** of completing it, the employee must repay **50%** of the cost.
The amount is deducted from the final salary where possible.
When employment ends, any accrued but unused annual leave for the current year is **paid out at the employee's basic daily rate** in the final salary.
